subject: Approve: B200 experimental profile gating + timeline (runtime 1.14 cut)
body:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, Dec 5, 2025 at 8:17 AM PT
Subject: Approve: B200 experimental profile gating + timeline (runtime 1.14 cut)
Attachments: B200_profile_gating_onepager_v3.pdf

Ava,

Requesting leadership approval to proceed with B200 experimental profile gating + timeline for runtime 1.14.

Summary:
- Default behavior: B200 tuned profile remains OFF unless explicitly enabled (feature flag + allowlist by pool).
- Enablement scope: single canary pool in us-east only. No EU enablement until driver/CUDA assumptions are stable.
- Rollback: pool-level disable (no new runtime build), plus “force baseline profile” override.

Timeline constraints:
- We need a clear go/no-go today so we can hit the 1.14 branch cut next week (targeting Dec 12).
- Infra has limited B200 nodes; validation will run with partial fleet access and higher variance than H100/L40S.

Asks:
1) Approval to ship code paths in 1.14 behind experimental gating.
2) Confirmation that we’re aligned on documentation requirements + oncall readiness criteria (below).

Proposed requirements before first enablement:
- Confluence: B200 reference page explicitly labeled EXPERIMENTAL, with fallback plan + known failure modes.
- Runbook: exact steps to disable per pool/region and how to confirm effective profile.
- Canary gates: hard bounds for p95 latency and error rate regression.

Thanks,
Neha

—
Neha Kapoor
Reliability / SRE
Redwood Inference



From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, Dec 5, 2025 at 9:06 AM PT
Subject: Re: Approve: B200 experimental profile gating + timeline (runtime 1.14 cut)

Approved with conditions.

We can ship the B200 profile selection code in 1.14 ONLY if the following are true:

1) Gating / defaults
- Default OFF everywhere.
- Enablement requires *both* (a) feature flag and (b) explicit per-pool allowlist.
- If GPU detection is ambiguous (SKU string variants, MIG, etc.), it must fall back to H100/L40S baseline behavior, not “best guess.”

2) Documentation / wording
- All docs must use “expected behavior” language and clearly state EXPERIMENTAL. No implied SLA.
- Document the minimum supported software stack assumptions (driver/CUDA/etc.) and what happens if those aren’t met.

3) Rollback / operational control
- Oncall must be able to disable B200 experimental profile within minutes at pool-level without a new deployment.
- Provide a single place to confirm: selected profile, override source, and key knob values (logs/metrics). If that’s not in 1.14, we should not enable.

4) Timeline clarity
- Code can land by 1.14 cut, but first enablement is contingent on a readiness review (you + runtime owner) and a clean canary. No “auto-enablement.”

Reply with the proposed rollback thresholds and the exact “disable” steps we’re standardizing, and I’ll consider this final.

Ava

—
Ava Chen
VP Engineering, Platform & Runtime
Redwood Inference



From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, Dec 5, 2025 at 10:02 AM PT
Subject: Re: Approve: B200 experimental profile gating + timeline (runtime 1.14 cut)
Attachments: B200_rollout_checklist_2025-12-05.docx

Thanks — aligned. Proposed rollback thresholds + disable steps below (also captured in attached checklist draft).

Rollback thresholds (any of the below sustained for 10 min in canary pool):
- p95 end-to-end latency: +10% vs baseline (same workload matrix bucket)
- 5xx / runtime error rate: +0.20% absolute (or +2x if baseline <0.1%)
- OOM / evictions: any increase that impacts success rate or causes >1% retries
- Streaming stability: any increase in stream aborts >0.10% absolute

Disable steps (standardized):
1) Flip pool config: b200_experimental_profile_enabled=false
2) Set force_profile=baseline (to avoid detection edge cases)
3) Confirm via metrics + logs:
   - metric: runtime_profile_selected{pool=…, sku=…}
   - metric: runtime_profile_override_source{…}
   - startup log line: “Profile compatibility matrix …”
4) Validate impact within 5–10 min on the canary dashboard panels.

On the gating mechanics:
- Agree on “two keys” (flag + allowlist). Code path will treat anything not explicitly allowed as baseline.
- We’ll explicitly block EU pools via config (separate allowlist) until the driver/CUDA constraints are met.

Readiness review:
- We’ll schedule a 15-min go/no-go with you on the day we propose first enablement (separate from the 1.14 branch cut).

Let me know if you want tighter thresholds; these are conservative given the variance on the partial B200 fleet.

Neha



From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, Dec 5, 2025 at 10:37 AM PT
Subject: Re: Approve: B200 experimental profile gating + timeline (runtime 1.14 cut)

These thresholds are fine.

Two additional requirements before first enablement:

- Comms: send a short note to eng-oncall + runtime oncall channel with (a) what changed, (b) how to detect profile-related regressions, and (c) the single “turn it off” switch.
- Evidence: attach or link a one-page canary report (before/after) with p50/p95 + error rate + retries + GPU mem headroom. Keep it small.

If we can’t meet the observability “confirm effective profile” requirement (metrics/logs) in 1.14, we still ship the code behind the flag, but we do NOT enable anywhere.

Proceed.

Ava



From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, Dec 5, 2025 at 11:42 AM PT
Subject: Re: Approve: B200 experimental profile gating + timeline (runtime 1.14 cut)

Understood — we’ll incorporate both requirements.

Next steps (today/this week):
- Update rollout runbook with the standardized disable steps + thresholds.
- Ensure runtime PR includes metrics/logs to confirm effective profile + override source.
- Draft the eng-oncall comms template and keep it ready for enablement day.
- Prepare the 1-page canary report format aligned with the perf-canary gates.

I’ll follow up once the runbook + metrics PRs are in review.

Neha
